offence_severity: Life imprisonment and fine of Rs.2000/- with default sentence for murder (Section 302 IPC) and rigorous imprisonment for two years and fine of Rs.1000/- with default sentence for the offence punishable under the Arms Act (Section 25 of Arms Act)
physical_harm: The deceased suffered a lacerated wound on the left side of the chest, piercing the left lung and damaging a major blood vessel, leading to death due to shock and haemorrhage.
number_of_offences: Seven offences/counts charged; five were finally upheld, two were confirmed as convictions
key_evidence_accepted: The presence of finger prints on the glass tumblers corroborates the testimonies of the eye-witnesses. The Fingerprint Expert reached the occurrence place on the occurrence day itself and raised the finger impressions on the two glass tumblers and duly packed them with his seal and date and handed over the same to the investigating officer for onward transmission to the finger print bureau.
witness_credibility: The presence of PWs 1 and 2 being the family members in the house is natural and the occurrence had taken place in the early morning hours. Their testimonies are cogent, natural and trustworthy. Moreover, there is no material discrepancy in their testimonies. The Courts below have rightly relied on their testimonies.
bail_history: Bail granted to the appellant/accused Surjit Singh in Criminal Appeal no. 2328 of 2009 shall be cancelled
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 10.11.2002; Trial judgment: 17.09.2007; High Court decision: 17.09.2007; Supreme Court decision: 17.12.2014
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court: C. NAGAPPAN, J. (Judgment delivered by); learned Addi. Advocate General of Punjab; learned Counsel for the convicted appellants; learned counsel for the respondents/acquitted accused
investigation_status: FIR registered (Exh. PN2); charge sheet filed; trial completed
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction of all seven accused; High Court: Acquitted five accused, confirmed conviction of two accused; Supreme Court: Affirmed conviction of two accused, acquittal of five accused
prosecution_argument: The prosecution case against the accused is supported by evidence of eye-witnesses who are further corroborated by the evidence of finger-print expert. The presence of PWs 1 and 2 being the family members in the house is natural and the occurrence had taken place in the early morning hours. Their testimonies are cogent, natural and trustworthy. The evidence of presence of finger-prints on the glass tumblers corroborates the testimonies of the eye-witnesses. The Courts below have rightly relied on their testimonies and the conviction and sentence imposed on the convicted appellants does not call for any interference.
defence_argument: The learned counsel appearing for the convicted appellants contended that PW1 Balwinder Kaur had not named the accused persons in her complaint and has only stated that two assailants after killing her son ran away from the place of occurrence. They also argued that the specimen finger impressions were not taken before the Magistrate in accordance with Section 5 of the Identification of Prisoners Act and it is unsafe to accept the evidence led in this regard. Another contention was raised that the presence of PWs 1 and 2 in their house on the occurrence day is doubtful since they would have gone far away to village Landey for attending the marriage of daughter of Satnam Singh's maternal uncle.
legal_principle_applied: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the presence of PWs 1 and 2 being the family members in the house is natural and the occurrence had taken place in the early morning hours. Their testimonies are cogent, natural and trustworthy. Moreover, there is no material discrepancy in their testimonies. The Courts below have rightly relied on their testimonies and the conviction and sentence imposed on the convicted appellants does not call for any interference.
precedent_relied_upon: Mohd. Aman and Anr. vs. State of Rajasthan (1997) 10 sec 44
sentencing_rationale: The final sentence was imposed as the conviction order against two accused is affirmed. The prosecution case against them is supported by evidence of eye-witnesses who are further corroborated by the evidence of finger-print expert. The Courts below have rightly relied on their testimonies and the conviction and sentence imposed on the convicted appellants does not call for any interference.
other_sentence_order: The bail granted to the appellant/accused Surjit Singh in Criminal Appeal no. 2328 of 2009 shall be cancelled and he is directed to surrender before the Additional Sessions Judge, Ludhiana to serve out the remaining sentence, failing which the learned Additional Sessions Judge is requested to take him into custody and send him to jail to serve his left over sentence.
